transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-10-14 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Ari Wolfe (Redwood AE), Samir Kapoor (Redwood SE), Dana Ortiz (MediSolve - Product), Leo Zhang (MediSolve - ML Eng), Priya Menon (MediSolve - CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be noisy):
- Reviewed pilot metrics from last 7 days: 98th pct latency spikes, partial KV cache hit rate, cost delta across quantized variants.
- Agreed on prioritized model candidate list and soft-fallback orchestration plan.
- Next steps: shared latency/cost doc, run latency sweep on dedicated pool, provide canonical prompts, schedule rollback tabletop.

---

[00:00] Ari (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, I see we're all here, uh, quick check - is this still a 40 minute slot?
[00:07] Priya (MediSolve - CTO): yes 40, we've got about 42 on the calendar, but good, we can overrun by a couple.
[00:12] Ari: great. quick round: samir from our side will drive the model perf bits. samir?
[00:16] Samir (Redwood SE): hey, thanks. i pulled up the last 7-day run, i know leo sent some logs yesterday, i've combined them with our prefix cache telemetry. some initial takeaways before we dive in: cache hit rate is about 62% for conversational flow A, but for batch reports it's down to 18% so that's why we're seeing token spend balloon on that route.
[00:37] Leo (MediSolve): yeah that's right, the report generation flow has lots of unique contexts so the cache doesn't help much. we're still tuning prompt templates to canonicalize the leading context.
[00:48] Dana (Product): quick context for anyone new, the two priority user journeys are: 1) triage chat (low latency, multi-turn) and 2) daily compliance report generator (high throughput, cost sensitive).
[01:05] Samir: perfect, and given that split we recommended two model classes: a smaller low-latency LLaMA-2-13B quantized variant for triage chat, and a larger 33B-ish open checkpoint for reports where quality matters but we can batch. that is the current candidate list.
[01:25] Priya: the management question is rollouts — we can't afford customer-facing regressions. how do we pin and then safely unpin if something goes sideways?
[01:33] Ari: yes this is the pinning gating question. our suggested pattern is: pin a version for 90% traffic, keep 10% shadowed to the previous model or to a conservative instance. we can do canary + soft fallback: if latency or response-quality regression above thresholds, traffic shifts automatically.
[01:50] Leo: can you define thresholds? like latency p95 above X ms? what's X here?
[01:56] Samir: in staging on dedicated GPUs we saw p95 around 180ms for the 13B quantized under your sequence distribution. for production we'd want a p95 SLO of 250ms for triage chat. fallback trigger if p95 > 300ms for two consecutive minutes or if hallucination/regression metric drops below the threshold on our eval set.
[02:20] Dana: small note — our legal team is insisting on auditability, so any automatic fallback must log the reason with request id and be visible in your console. can you do that?
[02:30] Ari: absolutely, the console emits per-request traces and reasons for routing decisions — we can add a short tag to auto-fallback events. will include example logs in the security doc I'm sharing.
[02:40] Priya: what about the rollback runway? if a model is pinned and we unpin, how fast can we get to a known-good variant — and what does state look like for KV cache?
[02:50] Samir: good question — KV cache is per model family and per sequence keying strategy. when we pivot to a different model family, KV cache warmup is cold; we recommend a staged traffic drain where we direct a small percent of requests to the new model and prime caches via shadow traffic. for emergency rollbacks between compatible variants (same family/quant) it's near instant; cross-family is slower and we recommend pre-warming with synthetic warmup jobs.
[03:18] Leo: synthetic warmup, got it — do you have tooling? we can run it ourselves?
[03:22] Samir: yes we provide a warmup harness, it's in the playbook link — the script takes a prompt corpus and streams to the endpoint with correct tokenization to populate KV caches. i'll share the link.
[03:30] Ari: i'd like to pivot to prioritization — we can't validate everything at once. samir, from your perf sweep what should we prioritize next week?
[03:38] Samir: prioritize the triage chat path on the 13B quantized candidate: it's the highest pang for latency and is expected to remove cost pressure if caching improves. second is stress-testing the 33B batch path with 500 concurrent batched jobs to see tails. third is the safety/regression evals on the canonical prompts leo will provide.
[03:58] Leo: ok i'll assemble the canonical prompts today, three per journey, including edge-case medical jargon, and label expected answer structure — e.g., for triage we want concise diagnosis likelihood and follow-up suggestion.
[04:12] Dana: can we talk about security — KMS integration and data residency? we need keys to never leave our VPC and logs retained in our S3 for 7 years per compliance.
[04:22] Ari: for Private deployment we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and VPC endpoints; audit logs can be shipped to your S3 or to our enterprise log retention module. for hosted/API flows, we manage key wrapping but we can support bring-your-own-key with HSM. i'll attach the security slide and the SOC2 snapshot.
[04:41] Priya: will your automatic batching and caching keep any customer data outside their control during prefetch/warmup? we've had concerns about synthetic warmup traffic touching production content.
[04:51] Samir: warmup can be run in isolated staging clusters that mimic production. we don't need production PII to warm caches; synthetic or redacted corpora work fine. when pre-warming cross-family we recommend redacted corpora.
[05:05] Dana: good. on to cost: we saw a 2.4x token cost increase last week for the report flow. is that purely cache miss and model size?
[05:13] Samir: mostly cache miss and the fact the 33B unquantized reference was invoked for some requests. we can push a quantized 33B or a 16-bit mixed variant that offers a 30-40% cost win at small quality delta. we included cost columns in the doc i'm going to share.
[05:29] Ari: i'll summarize a concrete rollout proposal: week 1 (this week) — pin 13B quantized for triage 10% canary, shadow previous at 90% to collect evals; run warmup for 24 hours. Week 2 — increase to 60% if metrics stable; in parallel run 33B quantized for batch in a dedicated pool and test concurrency. Week 3 — perform tabletop rollback drill and finalize SLA language.
[05:52] Priya: timeline seems ok but we need exact SLO numbers and a clear escape hatch. if we flip and the model regresses on NLU, we want automatic fallback plus human alert.
[06:02] Samir: escape hatch: routing policy with three tiers — green (normal), amber (degrade to lower-capacity variant with low-latency), red (route to previous stable model and page on-call). amber triggers for mild degradation, red for sustained regression or safety violation. all events emit traces and trigger alerts.
[06:21] Leo: can you give a concrete example? like thresholds and actions?
[06:25] Samir: sure: example — if regression metric drops by 8% compared to baseline over a 5-minute window -> amber: route 30% traffic to fallback for 5 minutes and run auto-eval. if regression persists > 10 minutes or p95 spikes 2x -> red: immediate 100% reroute to previous pinned model and page SRE.
[06:44] Priya: that helps. next, about compatibility matrix: are you maintaining a catalog that shows which model variants are compatible for instant rollback?
[06:53] Ari: yes, our model catalog includes compatibility tags (same family/quant/seq-len). we maintain a compatibility matrix and an emergency swap playbook. samir will attach the current CSV.
[07:04] Dana: regarding metrics we want to see: p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost per request, cache hit rate, hallucination score, and throughput. also request ids for any fallback events.
[07:15] Ari: noted, we'll add all those into the weekly dashboard and expose a filtered view for your SRE.
[07:20] Leo: quick note about logs — when automatic fallback happens, we want the original request and both model outputs for debugging, is that feasible?
[07:27] Samir: yes we can capture both outputs for a short retention window and redact PII per your policy. retention window configurable.
[07:34] Priya: any blockers for the pilot expansion?
[07:36] Ari: the remaining blockers are: 1) we need the canonical prompts (leo), 2) we need access to a staging environment for warmup (MediSolve infra), 3) legal sign-off on the audit log retention config.
[07:49] Dana: legal is reviewing, KMS questions remain but they seem solvable.
[07:53] Ari: good. Samir, anything else on performance?
[07:55] Samir: one more note — during load tests we saw rare GPU OOM when sequence length went beyond 3k tokens on the 33B; we recommend either a max-seq truncate or split strategy in the client to avoid OOMs during peak backfilling. i've put mitigation steps in the doc.
[08:15] Leo: ok we'll implement client-side truncation for long document ingestion.
[08:18] Ari: wrap-up, let's quickly confirm owners and dates.
[08:21] Ari: Samir will run the 1k-request latency sweep and upload traces (due 10/19).
[08:27] Samir: yep.
[08:28] Ari: Leo will send canonical prompts (due 10/18).
[08:31] Leo: on it.
[08:32] Ari: Priya / Dana — legal/KMS sign-off target 10/22?
[08:36] Priya: we'll try for that.
[08:38] Dana: yes, aim for 10/22.
[08:40] Ari: i'll send the security slides and the latency/cost spreadsheet by EOD 10/16.
[08:45] Ari: last quick question from me — are we ok with the proposed soft-fallback orchestration where we can do 30% amber routing automatically? any objections?
[08:52] Priya: no objections; just ensure humans are notified before a full cutover.
[08:56] Dana: agreed.
[08:58] Ari: perfect, we'll follow up in slack and i'll post the links to the doc set (playbook, catalog csv, security slides).
[09:05] Priya: thanks everyone.
[09:06] Meeting end.
